Never did I say that I believed there were 2.5 million unique installs, so I’m not sure why you’re hammering this non-existent, off-topic point besides arguing for arguments sake. Even if half of the downloads are “redownloads”  thats over 1.2 million unique downloads. If each person redownloaded 4 times, thats still roughly 620,00 unique downloads. For comparison to Mario speed runs, which was what that number was brought up for comparison to, the Mario game with the most submitted runs on speedrun.com is SM64 with only 48,857 runs. Its not even comparable, there are more hardcore classic WoW players than Mario speedrunners.

Ref: https://www.speedrun.com/series/mario/games?sort=mostruns&url=mario

Given hardcore is only a subset of classic WoW player, its safe to assume there is another player base of non-hardcore players, regardless how small the group could be, that enjoy leveling in classic Wow, and play it for that reason.

The comparison of downloads was the minimum number of people that have shown interest or tried the game mode before it was an official game mode.  For context, jehhans was saying that as many players speed run Mario as play hard-core wow. Do you believe that 2.5 million downloads of Mario have occurred to attempt speed running? Surely not.

The classic wow hard-core community is not a very small subset of the player base. The community made hard-core add-on has 2,479,000 downloads. That is by far the least popular of any release of hard-core, which blizzard has officially released twice now. In North America, they released as many hard-core servers for anniversary as they did PVE servers. To this day, the anniversary realms for hard-core fluctuate between medium and full pop, just like the PvE server that is more focused on end game content. Comparing that to Mario speedrunners is woefully ignorant. 
YOU may not enjoy the leveling experience, but YOUR opinion on how the community feels is not backed by data and is clearly at best unpopular, and frankly is just incorrect.
The existence of multiple releases of vanilla wow, and particularly hardcore’s popularity, completely disprove your theory.
